title: Canonical comparison of computing resolution classes with derived sections homology
statement: Let X be a scheme with its module-sheaf derived category in universe u. For every module sheaf F and nonnegative n, there is a linear equivalence e(F,n) from moduleCohomology^n(X,F) [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] to H^n of the unbounded derived global sections of F[0] [lem-sc-module-cup-naive-derived-compatibility]. For every computing resolution D of F [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data] and natural-degree kernel cycle a, there is an integer-degree cycle z in global sections of D.integerComplex [def-sc-module-cup-realization-complex-data]. Under the section map of extendXIso its component is a.val. The value e(F,n)(D.class n a) is H^n of the composite of moduleCup_globalComparison with RΓ(inv D.derivedAugmentation), applied to the localized cycle class of z [lem-sc-module-cup-derived-homology-tensor]. Equivalently Nonempty CupDerivedClassComparison X.

source.place: Section 20.31, identification H^n(X,F)=H^n(RΓ(F)); computing injective module resolutions in Section 20.11

proof.text: Extend an injective resolution I of F by zero. Its bounded-below complex of injectives is K-injective, so the right-derived comparison unit is invertible. The augmentation is inverted by Q. Compose their homology isomorphisms, homologyFunctorFactors and extension homology with I.isoRightDerivedObj to obtain the equivalence e in the displayed direction.

Extend the comparison from D.K to D.I.cocomplex by zero. The equation D.over identifies the localized augmentation composites, and naturality of the comparison unit identifies the resulting cohomology transport. The global homology map followed by inverse isoRightDerivedObj is exactly D.class; D.computes makes it an isomorphism. Extension cycles isomorphisms produce z with the displayed component. Naturality of homology projection gives the class equation. The identification is independent of the injective resolution by homotopies of comparison maps over F. Degree zero uses a zero incoming differential in both shapes.
